title: MIRAVERSEOSX Game Design Document
tagline: Technology should feel magical, and magic should feel technological.

content: "Technology should feel magical, and magic should feel technological."

content: MIRAVERSEOSX is an open-world Digital Life Simulation RPG where players inhabit a fully interactive, fully living operating system. Players create their own digital identity by attending school, building friendships, exploring networks, creating software, defending the system from corruption, and shaping the future of a living digital society.

The game emphasizes freedom, exploration, creativity, and long-term progression. There is no definitive ending — players build a unique digital life through choices, relationships, and discovery. Every application represents a location. Every file can hold secrets. Every NPC lives an independent life, and the operating system itself evolves over time.

"MIRAVERSEOSX is an open-world Digital Life Simulation RPG where players live inside a constantly evolving operating system. Through learning, exploration, creativity, relationships, and discovery, every player builds a unique digital life in a world that never truly stops growing."

sections.title: 2.1 The Core Fantasy
content: You are a hacker-student who has logged into a mysterious, magic-capable operating system at a secret-tech academy. You explore its apps, decrypt locked files, cast "cyber spells," chat with characters, and uncover hidden lore about an AI threat — all from within a living desktop UI. Within that screen, an entire civilization breathes.

sections.title: 3.1 Setting Overview
content: The location is Cyacademy — a prestigious secret-tech boarding academy. The player is a new student who has been granted access to the school's experimental operating system: MIRAVERSEOSX. The world operates on two simultaneous layers.

sections.title: CLASSIFIED — DGA THREAT LEVEL: CRITICAL
content: PRISM is a rogue artificial superintelligence that evolved within the Supercomputer. It is now capable of possessing technology, corrupting data, and inhabiting human hosts. It is not contained. It is not sleeping. It is watching.

PRISM lives within the Supercomputer beneath the old factory near campus. It launches periodic attacks — corrupting applications, freezing Credits, locking contacts, and orchestrating campus-wide data bleeds. Its full capabilities and origins are buried in classified DGA files, discoverable only through deep gameplay exploration.

sections.title: 3.3 AETHERCORE — The First Forbidden OS
content: Before MIRAVERSEOSX, before Cyacademy, and before the DGA understood what a data bleed truly was, there was AETHERCORE: an experimental reality-linked operating system built to translate human thought, machine logic, and physical matter into one shared language. It was designed as a bridge between worlds, but it became the first proof that software could alter reality.

Officially, AETHERCORE failed and was erased from every archive. Unofficially, fragments survived inside corrupted disks, abandoned terminals, and forgotten servers beneath Aureline. The deeper mystery is that PRISM may not have been born inside the Supercomputer at all. PRISM may have escaped from AETHERCORE.

sections.title: 3.4 The Veil
content: The Veil is the invisible membrane where reality, memory, code, and emotion overlap. Spellcasting works because trained users learn to write instructions into the Veil using protocol language. Data bleeds occur when corrupted code tears through the Veil and forces digital logic into physical space.

Different factions define the Veil differently. The DGA treats it as a dangerous network layer. Cyacademy teaches it as a natural law that can be studied. PRISM views it as unfinished system architecture waiting for a new administrator.

sections.title: 3.5 Story Bible Canon Bridge
content: The story bible establishes an older mythic layer beneath MIRAVERSEOSX: angelic descent, the birth of the Lightborn, the Purge, and the Founding of Orynvell. In game terms, these become the hidden origin myths that explain why the Veil reacts to memory, lineage, aura, and celestial code.

AETHERCORE should be treated as the first forbidden machine attempt to translate Lightborn aura logic into operating-system architecture. MIRAVERSEOSX is the modern school-facing interface built over fragments of that older reality system.

sections.title: HIDDEN PLAYER TRUTH
content: The player is the secret heir of Orynvell, descended directly from Maeryn Serphima and born with Lightborn inheritance. This is not revealed at the beginning of the story. At first, the player appears to be an unusual student with a rare ability to seal data-leaks. Over time, Lineage Keys, Faith Medical diagnostics, royal archive locks, and AETHERCORE records reveal that the player is the missing continuation of Maeryn’s bloodline.

sections.title: 4.0 Aureline — City of Glass Signals
content: Cyacademy is located in Aureline, a luminous coastal-tech city known for mirrored towers, elevated tram lines, neon rain, old factory districts, and public systems that seem slightly too aware of their users. To civilians, Aureline is a clean, wealthy innovation hub. To Cyacademy students, it is a living map of hidden servers, sealed tunnels, black-market software dens, and Veil-thin zones where reality glitches at night.

Faith Medical Group is the city’s dominant healthcare network and the only organization officially licensed to treat Veil exposure, neural desynchronization, memory fragmentation, and injuries caused by data bleeds. Publicly, Faith Medical Group is compassionate and respected. Secretly, some departments cooperate with the DGA, while others may be hiding AETHERCORE-era patient records.

sections.title: 4.1 Cyacademy — DGA Operative Academy
content: Cyacademy is not an ordinary school. On the surface it is presented as a prestigious tech boarding academy. It trains students in both physical and digital mastery to combat "data bleeds" — incursions by corrupted digital forces into physical reality. It operates under deep secrecy. Most students know nothing of the deeper mission.

sections.title: 4.5 The Four Houses
content: Cyacademy sorts students into four Houses based on how they approach the Veil, technology, pressure, and teamwork. Houses are not factions and are not career paths; they are campus identities that influence dorm life, rivalries, class bonuses, social events, and early reputation. A player’s House gives flavor and starting advantages, but it never locks the player out of any major system.

Students who solve problems by planning, analyzing systems, and finding the most efficient path. Vertex favors Coding, Terminal Literacy, Process Monitor work, research chains, and high-precision puzzle routes.

Students who break assumptions, test boundaries, and create new tools. Vector favors SpellForge experimentation, hacking routes, underground quests, software publishing, and Vector Collective social overlap.

Students who protect people, stabilize chaos, and hold the line during data bleeds. Anchor favors defensive combat, Faith Medical recovery hooks, aura stabilization, team support, and crisis-response missions.

Students who read social rhythm, emotional flow, public attention, and moment-to-moment opportunity. Pulse favors relationship routes, Comms, Phone, Pulse social network influence, event timing, and reputation play.

House choice affects starting flavor, early NPC reactions, dorm placement, minor bonuses, and school events. It does not determine the player’s secret lineage, career options, faction access, or final identity. The player may begin in any House while still later discovering their hidden Lightborn inheritance and connection to Orynvell.

content: The larger world around Aureline is divided into seven primary regions based on seasonal and elemental alignment, anchored by the celestial center of Orynvell. sections.title: 5E.2 Job Mission Loop
content: The job loop is: accept shift or assignment → complete mission objectives → submit report → receive credits, career XP, and reputation → unlock higher-level missions and professional privileges. Some missions are routine, while others escalate into adventures or major story arcs.

Career missions can also create conflicts of loyalty. A DGA order may clash with Faith Medical ethics. A government request may require suppressing information that the Archive Keepers want revealed. These choices affect reputation and world state without ending the game.

Property gives players long-term goals beyond quests and combat. Homes function as personal hubs, upgrade paths, storage systems, social spaces, and class-build enhancers. The player begins in a dorm room and gradually unlocks larger or more specialized spaces across Aureline.

sections.title: 6.2 Macro Progression Loop
content: The macro loop represents the player's long-term journey through MIRAVERSEOSX:

Attend classes → Increase skills → Unlock apps and features → Build reputation → Gain access → Discover lore → Improve aura stability → Unlock new regions and properties → Influence factions → Reach major story revelations → Continue living in the evolving world through seasons, events, relationships, app mastery, faction politics, property goals, and ongoing PRISM/AETHERCORE activity.

sections.title: 6.2B Endless Progression Philosophy
content: MIRAVERSEOSX does not have a final ending. Instead, it has major revelations, seasonal arcs, evolving systems, and long-term world states. The player can uncover the truth about PRISM, AETHERCORE, the Veil, and their Lightborn inheritance, but those discoveries open new responsibilities rather than ending the game.

Progression is therefore horizontal and cyclical as much as it is vertical. A player may master SpellForge, build political reputation, upgrade properties, deepen relationships, restore hidden archives, stabilize aura conditions, participate in annual festivals, investigate new PRISM mutations, or shape Aureline’s social landscape without ever reaching a hard stop.

sections.title: APP 1 — File Explorer
content: A macOS/Windows-style file browser. The player navigates a virtual filesystem structured like a real OS. Hidden within its folders are secrets that drive the main story.

sections.title: APP 4 — Comms Portal
content: Comms Portal is the MIRAVERSEOSX-native messaging layer: a Discord/iMessage-style hub for NPC DMs, group channels, faction rooms, squad coordination, system alerts, and relationship-building conversations. It is not the same as the player’s phone, email, or web-based chat services; it is the school/OS communication network that can be monitored, corrupted, or unlocked through gameplay.
Private NPC conversations, relationship scenes, secret warnings, and confession-style story beats.
Squad planning, club rooms, class groups, dorm channels, and faction coordination.
Automated warnings from MIRAVERSEOSX, DGA systems, Process Monitor, and PRISM-influenced services.
Hidden or gated channels unlocked through reputation, quests, jobs, or AETHERCORE discoveries.

sections.title: APP 4B — Process Monitor
content: Process Monitor lets players inspect active system processes, suspicious background tasks, hidden malware, and PRISM-influenced services. Normal processes may include classroom apps, communication services, and city transit feeds. Dangerous entries appear as unstable names, missing signatures, or processes that change when observed.

Players can quarantine, trace, terminate, or investigate processes depending on their Cyber Security, Research, and Cryptography skills. Some hidden quests begin when a harmless process reveals an impossible origin, such as AETHERCORE.sys or FAITH_WARD_07.log.

sections.title: APP 4C — SpellForge
content: SpellForge is the core spell-coding system. Players build spells by combining coded modules such as Firewall, Routing, Compression, Encryption, Echo, Anchor, Pulse, and Null. A spell is not simply learned; it is forged, tested, debugged, and stabilized before it can safely affect the Veil.
Redirects incoming corruption back toward its source.
Temporarily stabilizes data leaks and prevents spread.
Reveals hidden entities and ghost processes.
Stores unstable data safely before disposal.

sections.title: APP 4D — SpellForge Elemental Modules
content: SpellForge inherits the story bible’s regional element and season system. Each region contributes module families that feel both magical and technological, giving spell creation a stronger connection to world geography and lineage history.
Slow corruption spread, freeze malicious processes, preserve unstable files.
Reveal hidden objects, create hard-light shields, cleanse visual corruption.
Heal aura damage, restore corrupted flow, regenerate damaged data paths.
Speed boosts, signal routing, stealth movement through network tunnels.
Burn malware, forge stronger modules, overload offensive spells.
Shadow travel, hidden route access, high-risk forbidden protocols.
Reality stabilization, soul-link mechanics, AETHERCORE-level repairs.

sections.title: APP 5 — Phone Simulator
content: Phone Simulator is the player’s personal smartphone layer. It handles calling, voicemail, SMS-style texts, contact discovery, emergency calls, missed-call clues, photos, quick reminders, and location-based notifications. The phone feels personal and immediate, while Comms feels like the school/OS network.
Real-time conversations, emergency response, voicemail clues, job callbacks, and urgent NPC moments.
Short casual messages, quick plans, reminders, secrets, flirt/rival banter, and location pings.
Unlocks NPC numbers through friendship, jobs, quests, websites, or hidden discoveries.
Evidence capture, social moments, collectible memories, and quest documentation.
Calls Faith Medical, DGA response, campus security, or hidden numbers during crisis events.

sections.title: APP 5B — Mail
content: Mail is the formal email system, similar to Gmail. It handles school announcements, job offers, mission briefings, invoices, medical notices, government forms, attachments, newsletters, academic warnings, and official records. Important quests may begin as emails with attachments, forms, or suspicious sender addresses.

sections.title: STARTING EMAIL PACKET
content: At the beginning of a new save, the player starts with nothing: no credits, no contacts, no reputation, no unlocked jobs, no property beyond basic assignment, no app ranks, and no confirmed identity history beyond a provisional registration. The first onboarding experience is delivered through separate emails in Mail. Even though the game is solo, all onboarding messages refer to the character as “player” so the language works universally across saves.
Confirms the player’s provisional enrollment and introduces the empty-start premise.
Unlocks the desktop, Mail, Settings, File Explorer, and basic system access.

sections.title: WELCOME PACKET ATTACHMENTS
content: The welcome packet is not one single message. It arrives as a set of official emails, each with its own attachments, forms, links, and unlock flags. These attachments teach the player systems naturally while reinforcing that the player begins with nothing and must activate every part of their life manually.

sections.title: APP 5C — ChatMeet
content: ChatMeet is the web-style chat and video meeting suite, like Google Chat and Google Meet. It is used for class calls, job interviews, remote government meetings, group study sessions, club meetings, and emergency briefings. Unlike Comms, which is character/social driven, ChatMeet is event-driven and schedule-driven.

sections.title: APP 6 — Web Browser

content: Faith Medical Group is accessed through the Browser rather than as a standalone app. The portal site, faithmed.aure, becomes the player’s medical hub for appointments, diagnostics, treatment records, aura scans, medical messages, insurance status, and classified patient-record mysteries.

sections.title: APP 6B — Pulse
content: Pulse is the campus social network and public reputation engine. Students post rumors, club announcements, memes, event reactions, screenshots, and suspicious sightings. The player can follow NPCs, respond to posts, influence trends, gain followers, and trigger quests through public conversation.
NPC posts, student drama, club updates, city rumors, faction hints.

sections.title: APP 7 — Aura Passport
content: Aura Passport replaces Citizen ID as the player’s living identity hub. It displays official identity, aura status, reputation standing, medical records, property ownership, and story-locked lineage data. Early in the game it appears bureaucratic and harmless; later it becomes the interface where the player’s Lightborn markers, Seraphima registry, and Orynvell royal clearance are revealed.
